'''Tenno Jinja''' (天王神社、天王社) is a Shinto shrine dedicated to {{ill|Gozu Tennō|en|Gozu Tennō|qid=Q11570247|lt=Gozu Tennō}} and {{ill|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|en|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|qid=Q272993|lt=Susanoo-no-Mikoto}}, central deities in {{ill|Gion Faith|en|Gion cult|qid=Q11588425|lt=Gion Faith}}. This name is especially used for shrines in the lineage of {{ill|Tsushima Shrine|en|Tsushima Shrine|qid=Q705136|lt=Tsushima Shrine}} in {{ill|Tsushima, Aichi|en|Tsushima, Aichi|qid=Q816736|lt=Tsushima City, Aichi Prefecture}}. Other shrines based on Gion Faith include {{ill|Yasaka Shrine (disambiguation)|ja|八坂神社 (曖昧さ回避)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yasaka Shrine (disambiguation)|qq=}}, {{ill|Gion shrines|ja|祇園神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gion Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11588442}}, {{ill|Hiromine Shrine (disambiguation)|ja|広峯神社 (曖昧さ回避)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hiromine Shrine (disambiguation)|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, {{ill|Yakumo shrine|ja|八雲神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yakumo Shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11391847}}, {{ill|Suga Shrine|ja|須賀神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Suga Shrine|qq=}}, and {{ill|Susanoo Shrine|ja|素盞嗚神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Susanoo Shrine|qq=}}, whose usage varies by era and source.

Currently, only a few shrines still worship Gozu Tennō directly. Most shrines now enshrine {{ill|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|en|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|qid=Q272993|lt=Susanoo-no-Mikoto}}, who was syncretized with Gozu Tennō under {{ill|Shinbutsu-shūgō|en|Shinbutsu-shūgō|qid=Q2279088|lt=Shinbutsu-shūgō}}. During the {{ill|Shinbutsu bunri|en|Shinbutsu bunri|qid=Q1970535|lt=Shinbutsu bunri}} (separation of Shinto and Buddhism) in the {{ill|Meiji era|en|Meiji era|qid=Q3125096|lt=Meiji era}}, some shrines reverted to deities listed in ancient records other than Susanoo.

Since the Meiji period, many shrines have been merged with others or renamed to align with the Tsushima Gozu Tennōsha, such as renaming to {{ill|Tsushima Shrine|en|Tsushima Shrine|qid=Q705136|lt=Tsushima Shrine}}. As a result of Shinbutsu bunri and shrine mergers, some shrines now enshrine deities other than Gozu Tennō or interpret Gozu Tennō as a deity distinct from Susanoo. In some regions, the influence of these shrines can still be seen in place names incorporating "Tenno."
